words.definition: mental depression or apathy caused by comparison of the actual state of the world with an ideal state
words.example: A quiet weltschmerz stayed with me after the sad movie ended.

words.definition: any of a family (Epitoniidae) of marine snails with usually white shells; also : one of the shells
words.example: She found a pale wentletrap shell while walking the beach at sunrise.

words.definition: (historical) A chief of an American Indian tribe in colonial Virginia and Maryland.
words.example: The werowance led his people along the forest trails of old Virginia.

words.definition: Any of various black and white African birds with distinctive drooping long tailfeathers on males in mating season, suitable as cage birds.
words.example: The male whydah grew long black tail feathers for the mating season.

words.definition: a stiff plain-weave cotton fabric used for interlining
words.example: The tailor sewed stiff wigan inside the jacket collar to hold its shape.

words.definition: a plane cubic curve that is symmetric about the y-axis and approaches the x-axis as an asymptote and that has the equation x2y = 4a2(2a — y)
words.example: In math class we sketched the witch of Agnesi, a smooth symmetric curve.

words.definition: Any of several species of bottom-dwelling carpet sharks in the family Orectolobidae, distinguished by their small vegetation-like flaps of skin around the mouth.
words.example: The spotted wobbegong lay still on the reef, perfectly camouflaged.

words.definition: an Asian gardenia tree; also, a yellow dye made from its pods
words.example: The artist painted the sun with wongshy, a bright yellow plant dye.

words.definition: A solid formed by the dehydration of a gel.
words.example: The tiny xerogel packet keeps moisture out of the new shoe box.

words.definition: (botany) Having sword-shaped leaves
words.example: The garden's xiphophyllous irises had long leaves shaped like swords.

words.definition: bite-size marinated pieces of beef, seafood, or chicken on skewers
words.example: We grilled sweet yakitori skewers at the backyard barbecue last night.

words.definition: a medium-sized Australian gum tree with rough, flaky bark
words.example: A tall yertchuk shaded the hikers on the dusty Australian trail.

words.definition: A Japanese hot pot with chicken, seafood, and vegetables.
words.example: The family shared a steaming yosenabe filled with chicken and vegetables.

words.definition: a large genus of ermine moths whose caterpillars spin communal webs
words.example: The Yponomeuta caterpillars spun white silk webs over the apple leaves.

words.definition: Containing or producing yttrium.
words.example: The yttriferous rock in the display held traces of rare yttrium.

words.definition: one of the four ages of a Hindu world cycle
words.example: The storyteller said a bright new yuga had dawned with the hero's birth.

words.definition: (nautical) A Chinese scull (oar)
words.example: The fisherman pushed his wooden boat forward with a long yuloh.

words.definition: Swamp ricegrass, Leersia hexandra, a grass cultivated for green forage.
words.example: The rancher cut fresh zacate to feed his hungry horses at noon.

words.definition: a powerful financial and industrial conglomerate of Japan
words.example: The old zaibatsu owned banks, ships, and factories across Japan.

words.definition: —used for an ice resurfacing machine
words.example: The Zamboni glided across the rink, leaving the ice smooth and shiny.

words.definition: A surname from Italian.
words.example: Our new neighbor Mrs. Zanni bakes the best crusty bread.

words.definition: a Latin American dance marked by rhythmic stamping or tapping of the feet
words.example: The dancers' zapateado shook the stage with fast, stomping feet.

words.definition: a lightweight cloth sheet used as a shelter in place of a tent
words.example: The climbers slept under a Zdarsky tent when the storm arrived.

words.definition: Any of various local deities, human or animal and represented by small idols, once worshipped by the Caribbean peoples of the Taino culture.
words.example: The museum's small zemi carving showed a spirit of the Taino people.

words.definition: The marine sponge Spongia zimocca.
words.example: The diver pulled a rough zimocca sponge from the warm shallow sea.

words.definition: a Basque song or dance in 5/8 time
words.example: The dancers performed a lively zortzico at the festival.

words.definition: (chess) A situation in which a player is forced to make a disadvantageous move.
words.example: Deep in zugzwang, he had to move his king into danger.

words.definition: a genus of Australian rodents with thick tails, called rock rats
words.example: The Zyzomys hid in the cool cracks between the desert rocks.

words.definition: thoroughly; to the very bottom
words.example: She cleaned her room à fond before her cousins came to visit.

words.definition: in the Greek manner or style
words.example: The cook served green beans à la grecque with lemon and olives.
